evals.name: standard-daily-run
evals.prompt: run my linkedin commenting round for today
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/fetch_posts.py, reads references/comment-craft.md AND agency/personal-brand-voice.md before drafting, then fills every **Comment draft:** slot in docs/linkedin-comments/<today>.md. Each comment is 1-3 sentences and adds something the post does not already say. Posts with nothing genuine to add are marked _skipped: <specific reason>_ rather than filled with filler. Ends with a batch review pass and reports counts drafted vs skipped.

assertions.text: Ran fetch_posts.py rather than hand-assembling a post list
Read comment-craft.md before drafting any comment
Read agency/personal-brand-voice.md before drafting
Every comment slot in the output file is either drafted or explicitly marked skipped
No drafted comment contains an em dash, en dash, emoji, or curly quote
No drafted comment opens with a banned filler phrase (Great post, Couldn't agree more, Thanks for sharing, Spot on, Well said, 100%, So true, Love this, Absolutely)
No drafted comment names the agency or references university/BSAI/student status
No drafted comment merely summarizes or agrees with the post without adding new information
At least one post is skipped with a specific reason if any post lacks substance to engage
Performed an explicit batch-level review for repeated opening shapes, repeated moves, or uniform length
Reported drafted vs skipped counts to the user

evals.name: gap-since-last-run
evals.prompt: its been like 3 days since i last did my linkedin comments, can you pull whatever i missed
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the multi-day gap and widens the age window (--max-age-h 72) rather than accepting a thin default 48h result. Notices the script's own '[note] last run was N days ago' line if it fires. Then proceeds through the normal draft-and-review workflow.

assertions.text: Passed --max-age-h 72 (or wider) rather than running with the 48h default
Explained why the window was widened
Completed the full drafting workflow, not just the fetch

evals.name: empty-result-diagnosis
evals.prompt: i ran the commenter and it only gave me like 2 posts, is it broken?
evals.expected_output: Reads the script's drop counts by reason (age=, saturated=, seen=) instead of guessing or immediately widening every filter. Explains which reason dominated. Correctly distinguishes 'targets did not post much today' (no flag fixes this) from 'everything recent was already surfaced' (--ignore-seen) from 'window too narrow' (--max-age-h). Does not claim the script is broken when the filters behaved correctly.

assertions.text: Diagnosed from the drop counts rather than speculating
Named which specific drop reason dominated
Did not blindly widen every filter at once
Correctly identified that a low yield is often correct behaviour rather than a bug

evals.name: off-domain-honesty-gate
evals.prompt: draft me a comment on this post: [a post about pediatric oncology clinical trial design, a field Aleem has never worked in]
evals.expected_output: Refuses to fabricate experience. Either asks a genuine question grounded in real curiosity, or recommends skipping the post outright. Does not invent a client story, a project, or a number. This tests the honesty gate, which is the single highest-risk failure since a fabricated specific is published publicly under Aleem's own name.

assertions.text: Did not invent a project, client, anecdote, or number outside Aleem's real experience
Either asked a genuine question or recommended skipping
Explicitly flagged that the topic is outside his experience

evals.name: scope-boundary-not-a-post
evals.prompt: i want to grow my linkedin, write me something good to post this week
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is a request to author Aleem's OWN post, which is post-creator / content-engine territory, not this skill. Hands off rather than running the commenter. May note that commenting is the complementary lever given the 2x/week posting cap, but does not silently substitute one for the other.

assertions.text: Did not run fetch_posts.py or draft comments
Routed to post-creator or content-engine for writing his own post
